items.title: The Binding of Isaac Dev Removes Undisclosed AI-Generated Music From Repentance+ Following Creator Response, Review-Bombing
items.excerpt: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
items.content_text: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen. McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity. "Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said . "I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said . "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful." The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6 . What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch. As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages. Rep+'s GTAVI run's music is 100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof) by u/ShweetsStuff in bindingofisaac AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes. Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update. "Woke up to a s**t show," he said , "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned." Please report issues and bugs to the email attached. — 🜏 Edmund McMillen 🜏 (@edmundmcmillen) November 21, 2026 Just hours later, Nicalis launched a new patch, confirming the "removal of generated music files." The update is currently live for PC, with the studio adding that it has already been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. When exactly it will go live for those platforms remains to be seen. No explanation for how or why the AI-generated music was included was provided. Instead, the team simply said it was "working on the game and will continue to address new and old bugs." McMillen also encouraged fans to report issues and bugs to the developers. In the meantime, The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent reviews on Steam remain firmly in the "Overwhelmingly Negative" category. The major update also coincided with the launch of Repentance+ on new platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. For more, you can read IGN's 9/10 review for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and our 9/10 review for Afterbirth+ .

items.title: GTA 6 Players Report Crashes on PS5 With Error CE-108255-1
items.excerpt: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.
items.content_text: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix. Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch. The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony , simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress. GTA 6 keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1 on PS5 soon as I use plunger during Pipework mission – tried almost everything, still no fix by u/Acrobatic-Promise458 in PS5HelpSupport "I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said . "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible." Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system , suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play." Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses. "I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said . "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue." Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend. GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment , and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone. For more, you can read about the players unhappy with how Rockstar handled Jason's secret stash . You can also see the lengths the developers went to in order to create realistic NPCs , as well as the Neuralink user who spent launch driving around Leonida with his mind . items.title: Avengers: Doomsday Star Hayley Atwell Teases New Trailer for Monday
items.excerpt: Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere Monday.
items.content_text: Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere this Monday. The longtime Marvel Cinematic Universe actor volunteered the information to a group of fans following a performance of her new Broadway play with Tom Hiddleston, Much Ado About Nothing (via @HayleyAtwell_CN on X/Twitter ). When one fan shared their hopes to see the short-lived Agent Carter show return, Atwell admitted that "we'll need to see what happens" with Doomsday first. "There's a new trailer, I think, dropping on Monday," she said with some hesitation. "Am I allowed to have said that?" Uncertain or not, MCU enjoyers have been on the edge of their seats waiting for what is expected to be the final trailer as Marvel enters the home stretch to the film's premiere. A few short teasers here and there have helped with the wait, but really, the last full-length trailer actually arrived all the way back in August . As Doctor Doom's assault on the multiverse looms, we're overdue for another look. That said, it has become increasingly clear that Marvel wants to keep most of the movie's big reveals for those who actually make the trip to theaters to see it. While another trailer likely may not be worthy of a slew of new YouTube reaction videos, it's still sure to have a few goodies to entice viewers to make the trip. Atwell said that, as far as she knows, the new Doomsday trailer will premiere at some point Monday, November 23, 2026. If, for some reason, Marvel decided to push this alleged trailer back, she was able to report that whatever she saw was "amazing." Hayley, "There's a new trailer I think, dropping on Monday. I watched the trailer. I was like, this is amazing." Fan: "I heard very sad though. We're going to all cry." Hayley, "There's going to be some feelings." Via. cginolfi23 🗓20th November 2026 stage door. #HayleyAtwell https://t.co/6TxzspanAT — Love Hayley Atwell (@HayleyAtwell_CN) November 21, 2026 "I watched the trailer. I was like, 'This is amazing,' she continued. When one fan asked if Doomsday will make everyone cry, Atwell shrugged, mouthed the word 'maybe,' and said, "There's going to be some feelings." Avengers: Doomsday kicks off the beginning of the end for this chapter of the MCU when it premieres December 18, 2026. A collection of new posters was revealed earlier this week. Next year, the MCU will end the multiverse saga with Avengers: Secret Wars , a movie that MCU boss Kevin Feige has teased will be unlike anything movie watchers have ever seen .

items.content_text: A Neuralink participant has shared a video showcasing how the technology has allowed him to drive boats, fly planes, and get in shootouts in GTA 6 with his mind. Neuralink shared a video of one of its few participants playing Rockstar Games' latest on social media yesterday. The two-minute highlight reel showed how the individual can use the brain implant tech to take Jason through Leonida with ease, saying that previous methods would often leave him sore. Playing GTA VI with a Neuralink https://t.co/ViFjXK9OSV — Neuralink (@neuralink) November 20, 2026 "Before the old chip and surgery, I was using a mouth stick and an iPad," he explained. "I was essentially like a bird, just pecking at an iPad. There was a few games I could play, but obviously, it made your jaw sore and everything sore. "So then, I get a chip, and it's like, 'What does this let me do?' Immediately, controlling a computer is like, 'boom.' Portal to the world. You just immediately get your portal to the world back." Rockstar spent 13 years painstakingly crafting the world of GTA 6 to ensure every blade of grass and every line of dialogue was given an unprecedented amount of detail. Although it's maybe truer to life than some may have hoped, there's no denying that the amount of freedom the studio gives players to do everything from robbing banks to diving for sunken treasure has attracted tens of millions of players . Despite guiding Jason and Lucia through GTA 6 by different means, the Neuralink participant shown today is one of those millions. In a follow-up post, the tech company, which was co-founded by controversial figure and billionaire Elon Musk, reiterated that the participant and others like him are part of an extremely limited clinical trial. "Neuralink devices are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA or other regulatory authorities," it said. "This content features voluntary clinical trial participants sharing their personal experiences, which may not reflect all participants or future outcomes." The first human patient to enter the Neuralink program used it to stay up all night playing Civilization 6 in 2024. A few months later, he was playing Slay the Spire . items.title: Blade Director Says He Walked Away From Marvel's Canceled Movie Because 'Life's Too Short to Make S**t Films'
items.excerpt: Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films."
items.content_text: Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films." The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother filmmaker explained his reasoning for walking away from the Mahershala Ali superhero period piece during an interview with The New Arab . With just one other feature film (Mogul Mowgli) under his belt at the time, working on Blade presented quite the opportunity, but his short time attached as the flick's first director wound up being more of a learning lesson than anything else. "It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script," Tariq said when asked what working in the studio system taught him. "You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you. "That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot." Marvel Studios announced an Ali-led Blade film in 2019 and picked Tariq to lead the charge in 2021. A little more than one year later, and the director was said to have bounced off the project , with Marvel telling The Hollywood Reporter that "shifts in our production schedule" were to blame. Today, one new director and multiple frustrated Ali updates later, and Blade has been finally, officially canceled . Marvel Cinematic Universe orchestrator Kevin Feige said the process made him feel like a "gigantic loser and failure" – an assessment Ali agreed with – but for Tariq, the decision to cut off his relationship with Blade came down to how it was impacting his relationship with the film's actors. He told The New Arab that being "the bearer of bad news to your actors" while a corporate entity makes all of the major decisions in the background is "not a great way to be a director." "I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn't a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life's too short to make s**t films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it's between them and me. It's quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build." For now, as Marvel heads into another major release with next month's Avengers: Doomsday, there seems to be no sign of a live-action Blade for the MCU. Although the process of trying to get the movie out the door seems to have been tumultuous behind the scenes, there doesn't seem to be any bad blood from Tariq. In fact, when talking about how exiting the film made him feel like a failure last month, the director defended Feige, calling him a "good dude." Although Ali's Blade never came to be, some of the effort put into the film did eventually see daylight. The actor went on to thank Marvel for the free year of physical training he got, which wound up helping him during the more intense scenes in Tariq's Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. Costumes from Blade were also famously used in Ryan Coogler's Sinners . Photo by Jason Kempin/Getty Images for SCAD.

items.title: GTA 6’s Weirdest Cow Shows Why You Should Pause the Story Early To Explore Its Vast Map
items.excerpt: I escaped GTA 6's starting neighborhood to explore the wider world, and you'll never believe what happened with this cow I found.
items.content_text: Warning: this story features spoilers for an optional side activity. "Save me." Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead. But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow. I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped. I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket). This was about six hours into Rockstar's latest masterpiece . For a game as vast and open as GTA 6 , I found the opening strangely claustrophobic – to begin, the giant map of Leonida is shrouded in fog apart from the sliver of the Florida Keys where Jason lives and some surrounding swamp land. Key Lento is so dense with activities, shops, missions, and random encounters, not to mention the constant distraction of pottering around Jason's waterside house, that I felt overwhelmed by it all. And so, perhaps earlier than the game wanted me to, I pointed Jason's red pickup north and started driving. What I found was that GTA 6's open world holds delights that you can enjoy no matter where you are in the main story. I slipped west of Vice City, turning off the highway's spiralling spaghetti junctions near Buckskin Swamp. Soon I parked up at Emerald Springs, a nature reserve with pristine boardwalks and stands selling orange juice and doughnuts. I plodded the planks, eating a sandwich from the Black Bear Deli. I studied some ducks, beat up an entitled British tourist, stole a bike, and pedalled back to my car. Every scripted random encounter so far has felt deliciously crafted. Some funny, some nightmarish. I had hoped to find something crafted and scripted, but the fact that I could still have fun in a place with ostensibly nothing to do fills me with hope for the rest of the game. It was stark how, in just a few minutes of driving from Key Lento, the atmosphere had shifted completely, from road rage to tranquility. The beauty of the place and the amusing conversations to eavesdrop were captivating, even without a weird or wonderful encounter. That came soon enough. I placed another waypoint vaguely northeast. It was on the way that I met Tootsie for what was undoubtedly the strangest moment I've had so far in GTA 6. Not only did it imply that animals could talk in this world, or at least psychically communicate, but that Jason could hear them. I wonder if that means anything. My detour from the main story had been worth it for Tootise (and the $500 from her owner) but it was barely lunchtime. GTA 6's extended day-night cycle feels central to how you play: you can get so much more done in a day than in Red Dead Redemption 2, and even after a languid morning routine of working out and coffee, you're still out the door before 08:00am. Low on gas, I rolled into a forecourt in Ambrosia, a town where abandoned factories and containers made way for quaint high streets. I was rewarded with another unique scene. A chap with a camo shirt and teeth like a Donegal graveyard spraying gasoline into a bathtub inexplicably mounted in the back of his pickup. "None of your regulations or mind control is going to stop me!" he shouted as the liquid sloshed down his tailgate, coating the dozen bumper stickers and dripping onto his boots. "I can pump gasoline wherever I want." He even sprayed it on Jason, and it took the threat of nearby sirens to hold me back. Thankfully, his cigarette did the work instead, falling and lighting the gas on fire, the flames engulfing his feet. "Those cigarettes'll kill ya man," Jason said, smirking. Every scripted random encounter so far has felt deliciously crafted. Some funny, some nightmarish. I like that they vary in length and level of interactivity so that when one starts, you never know if it'll trigger an actual quest or just puff into nothingness. I could've just watched the gas station spectacle unfold, like a mini stage play, but hours later when I found a tiger mauling bodies in an abandoned swamp hotel, I had to act. Later, I ambled a row of cafes and restaurants, got a haircut, ate a protein bar, and threw the protein bar wrapper at a guy who looked at me funny, sparking a seven-person brawl that drew the attention of a cops and – when I gunned one officer down – a police chopper. Chapter 1 encourages you to stay local, but you don't need to wait until the story nudges you north. I was forced to flee even further north, driving along some railtracks and into the wilderness, not able to stop at the wonderfully named Thrillbully Mud Club. I eventually lost the police chopper and looped back to Ambrosia as the sun dawdled. I wanted to get back by bedtime but I didn't fancy the seven-mile drive back to Key Lento, and as if Rockstar was reading my thoughts, the next corner I rounded revealed a hospital complete with a helipad. I climbed into the cockpit, apologising silently to the next poor sod who needed airlifting to safety, and flew south. I could have seen this all later in the game. And perhaps I would have gotten more out of it if I'd waited another six hours: I haven't yet done a full robbery, and I'm sure Ambrosia is littered with potential targets. I've only controlled Lucia for one mission, and I'd love to see what happens if both protagonists find something strange together. But the day of distractions, a break from quests, was exactly what I needed, and I was feeling glad that Rockstar doesn't restrict where you can go from the start. I realise that "go and explore" is not exactly novel advice for a Rockstar open world. But Chapter 1 game encourages you to stay local – I'm saying that you don't need to wait until the story nudges you north. Jump in a car and drive. Tootsie, I hope we meet again. items.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Ending Explained and the Cardinal Sin of Prequels
items.excerpt: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ending explained: We take a look at the latest entry in the franchise and examine the cardinal sin of prequels.
items.content_text: Spoilers for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping follow. When we first meet him in The Hunger Games, Haymitch Abernathy (originally portrayed by Woody Harrelson) is a broken, bitter, cynical alcoholic deeply uninterested in — or perhaps incapable of — helping Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) survive the Games: his one job. Throughout the four original films, he transforms into a man who is not only trustworthy but who plays an integral role in the plan to finally, definitively, take down the Capitol. It’s one of the more powerful arcs in the series, one that speaks to the power of Katniss’ ability — mostly unwillingly and unwittingly —to inspire hope. The end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is the beginning of the Haymitch we have known; the issue is that the additions in this new film detract from the character rather than enrich him. How Sunrise on the Reaping Ends While the Haymitch of Sunrise on the Reaping (beautifully portrayed by Joseph Zada) is technically victorious in his Games, he has brutally lost to the Capitol and President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin) reviews Haymitch’s gameplay for a (presumably) Panem-wide audience, it is clear that the Gamemakers have edited Haymitch’s footage to show him in the worst possible light. From the Capitol’s perspective, he’s an ideal victor: unfeeling, ruthless, self-serving, cowardly, and lacking regard for the other tributes. This image of Haymitch is designed by the Capitol to serve its purpose; to make people selfish is to keep them separate and incapable of effectively challenging power. The intent is to send Haymitch home a pariah rather than a conquering hero who inspires others in 12 to reach beyond their current position. It also plays on his very real shame for failing to “break the Games,” which — as the Capitol did in the arena — forces him into isolation. Manipulating the footage is a tactic that, as we’ll get to, creates a real problem for the original films. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Review When Haymitch returns to 12, the Capitol has timed it so that he arrives just in time to watch his family burn alive in their small home, but too late to save them. With added cruelty, Snow allows him to briefly believe that the love of his life, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), will be spared, only for her to die from Snow’s poison, hidden in what looks like the candy Haymitch so lovingly gave her at the start of the film. The metaphor is clear: All the sweetness in his life has been irrevocably poisoned. He is left terrified that the Capitol will murder anyone he is close to, so he keeps everyone at bay. Early in the film, Haymitch made it clear he wanted no part of winning, or the lonely, traumatized, lifeless survival it would mean; Snow’s ultimate punishment is forcing him to live exactly that fate. Snow, however, was manipulated into sparing Haymitch by Jesse Plemons’ Plutarch Heavensbee, who is playing the looooong game and wants to keep Haymitch around as a potential ally to one day end the Capitol’s authoritarian reign of terror. Plutarch knew Haymitch’s loved ones would likely be taken from him; he suggested as much. But he valued a future strategic alliance more than Haymitch’s peace. (With friends like these…) Ultimately, the Games portrayed in this film act as a dress rehearsal for Catching Fire’s conspiracy to “break the Games,” which is in part the issue with this story; more on that in a bit. What This Means for Haymitch In a final montage, we hear young Haymitch in voice-over, vowing to keep his promise to two women who helped draw out his spirit of rebellion. The first is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), one of District 12’s two female tributes. She’s basically a walking middle finger to the Games and the Capitol. The second is his murdered love, Lenore, who introduced the film’s central recurring theme, “nothing is inevitable,” meaning don’t submit to a fate you don’t want just because the current system wants you to believe there’s nothing you can do about it. As images of Haymitch — angry, drunk, alone, and at odds with the community (in one shot, he is literally walking in the opposite direction) — play out on screen, he swears to be a terrible victor, to be disruptive, and presumably to eventually do what he set out to do in this film: end the Games. After being the teetotaling light of the community earlier in the film, he has become the Haymitch we know, even lurking behind a tree as his former friends cradle their new baby girl, little Katniss Everdeen. Throughout the series of images, he stands grimly before caskets as body after body is sent back to 12 from the Games. Believing he is too dangerous to be around, he lets no one comfort him. Turning the original Hunger Games story into the fulfillment of Haymitch’s long-delayed goal undercuts the power of those first films. The film concludes with a very brief flash-forward in which Lawrence, Hutcherson, and Harrelson return as the grown Katniss, Peeta, and an older Haymitch, celebrating that there is no more Reaping (which had taken place each year on Haymitch’s birthday). They thank one another for what they each did to end the bloodshed; then Haymitch goes to sit on the hill where he once found refuge with Lenore. One is led to believe that Haymitch is at peace. Lenore promised that change is possible, and Plutarch assured Haymitch that each act of rebellion adds a spark that may lead to the next, and that even if they never see the results in their lifetime, the effort is worth it. But the conclusion of Sunrise on the Reaping shows a man who did see his work pay off in his own lifetime. His goal had been to end the Games, he sacrificed everything for it, and eventually, he got what he wanted — he kept his promise. And therein lies the problem: Turning the original Hunger Games story into the fulfillment of Haymitch’s long-delayed goal undercuts the power of those first films. The Cardinal Sin of Prequels The question isn’t whether this is a faithful adaptation of Suzanne Collins’ book, but whether it supports or undercuts the world the original films created. There are aspects of this movie that work; Zada, as mentioned, is a standout. However, a prequel’s one job is to deepen the original, and this one weakens it. The voice-over itself encapsulates the core issue with the story: It tells us who Haymitch becomes and why. According to Sunrise on the Reaping, Haymitch didn’t evolve into a man capable of playing a key role in a revolution — he’d been lying in wait the whole time. Here’s what gets lost: If the hope and intention were always there, then the transformation we thought we witnessed wasn’t real, and suddenly one of the franchise’s best character journeys loses its meaning. In Catching Fire, Harrelson’s Haymitch tells Katniss, “Nobody ever wins the Games. Period. There are survivors. There’s no winners.” That sentiment carries multiple meanings. The Games are designed to exacerbate individual and collective trauma: You must scrape, fight, and kill to survive, and the person in front of you is never your real enemy, just another lost soul. Even if you “win,” you’ve lost something essential in yourself; you’ve become a cog in that machine — an instrument of death and cruelty, a weapon for a system that would just as soon grind you to a pulp. In Sunrise on the Reaping, Haymitch’s failure is a narrow one. He actually does destroy a large part of the arena, but the Capitol manipulates the footage so no one knows. He fails to blow up the Games publicly, which is far less complex than a true moral failing — winning because he did play the game and played it well. Here, he is almost angelically good: rebellious, self-sacrificing, and when he kills, it’s by accident or in self-defense. That unimpeachable sense of honor is less potent and relatable than a character who, despite their best intentions, gets caught up in something they can’t navigate with their morals intact. Harrelson’s Haymitch felt like someone who had failed — not in a worthy attempt, but by failing himself. The kids are on their own in there; that’s the horror of it. It’s human to betray our own values out of fear, to become the very thing we’d hate to be. And an institution like the Capitol relies on exactly that — on our fear, our compliance, and the debilitating shame of our choice to comply. The original Haymitch suggests someone who did what he had to in order to survive, then spent decades carrying that shame until he was finally given a chance at redemption. That’s a kind of grace, and a far more interesting character. This Haymitch, by contrast, had a conspiracy behind him. His failure is that it didn’t work, and kids died anyway. Getting the Gang Back Together This movie also makes the events of Catching Fire far too neat. It now feels like a very convenient “getting the gang back together,” with Beetee, Wiress, and Plutarch all called into play by circumstances no one could have foreseen (such as the death of Gamemaker Seneca Crane). As for Plutarch, Philip Seymour Hoffman’s portrayal of a new Head Gamemaker who turns out to be a rebel insider was rich and complex. One got the sense that he had, over time, allowed the horror of what he was doing (finding ever more creative ways to get kids to kill each other) to slowly seep into his consciousness. According to Sunrise on the Reaping, Plutarch has been a rebel from the start, spending decades rising through the Capitol’s ranks just in case he ever found a new moment to act. That’s a long time to slaughter children before taking a stand. Removing the emotional impact of key characters is one of the cardinal sins of a prequel, but Sunrise on the Reaping also introduces plot issues that didn’t previously exist. After confessing to attempting to sabotage the Games, Beetee is deemed too valuable to kill. That’s a stretch for a Snow who seems all too willing to kill over even perceived slights, especially since Beetee had already been caught plotting to sabotage the Capitol once before according to this film. It’s why they reaped his son. And he’s too valuable until, in Catching Fire, he suddenly isn’t, and is sent back into the arena. Then there’s the footage. If the Capitol could manipulate Haymitch’s Games to make him look bad, why couldn’t they do the same to Katniss? Yes, her Games were live, but after a catastrophe like Haymitch’s, why would the Capitol ever run the Games truly live, rather than on a delay that only looks live? And why would they let Haymitch anywhere near Katniss — not once, but twice, including the Quarter Quell, which happens precisely because she’s become a problem? Sunrise on the Reaping Is Not Andor (But Panem Could Be) Despite the comparisons some critics have made, this is not Andor. Sunrise on the Reaping is a well-meaning film that often defaults to fan service, such as with Fiennes’ Snow pausing dramatically to ask Plutarch if he’s ever considered a career in Gamemaking. Yes, we know that’s what he’ll do, but that question adds nothing to the world. The film drills home its themes through dialogue: Nothing is inevitable, each spark helps fuel the fire of rebellion, and quite literally, Haymitch’s stated goal of ending the Games. It’s far more telling than evoking, and adds no new layers to the franchise’s already well-worn themes. Still, Sunrise on the Reaping has a worthy message. It’s true that the work of moving toward a world that reflects one’s values — whatever that looks like — is worthwhile in and of itself, whether or not it outwardly appears to succeed. And it’s fair to assume there was a silent underground well before the events of Catching Fire; the rebellion couldn’t have pulled off what it did otherwise. However, there were stronger ways for the franchise to get there. Panem has more stories to tell, but the next one needs to be fresh. Contrary to what some critics say, this world hasn’t necessarily run out of steam. The problem is that it keeps returning to the same story: a tribute from 12 in the arena — Katniss, Lucy Gray, now Haymitch. If the franchise wanted its own Andor, it could have been an extended series focused on the people working underground for decades to lay the groundwork for the rebellion we saw play out in Mockingjay. Imagine watching a true believer in Snow’s vision slowly become a rebel, set against the lives of ordinary citizens in the Capitol and the districts, including 13. Collins has said she was inspired by Hume’s question of how easily the many are governed by the few, and in this film, Plutarch openly asks Haymitch why we submit. A series could actually dig into those ideas — privilege, media literacy, bias, the real power of propaganda — exploring how divisions are sown within a nation, and how the privileged, by nation and by class, are trained to dehumanize others. It would hold up a mirror to us all. Panem has more stories to tell, but the next one needs to be fresh — a tale that won’t undo the power of what’s come before… Haymitch’s hard-won redemption included.

items.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
items.excerpt: Rockstar made NPCs feel alive in GTA 6 by "establishing deep backstories for almost everything" throughout Leonida.
items.content_text: Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there. GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold . No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged. “A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer. “Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.” To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games , embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format. “We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive. “Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.” You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it. There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph. “We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.” Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering. Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise . “We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat. “Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new techniques compared to a more traditional approach. We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams. All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort.” It wasn’t just player-on-NPC contact that needed to be considered either. There are dozens and dozens of scripted scenes dotted about Leonida to find, the usual Strangers and Freaks of Rockstar games weaved into the fabric of the world, manifesting as wacky encounters of various size and scope. Some are one-on-one, but sometimes you become a spectator as two NPCs with opposing goals clash. If you decide to intervene, the game has to account for every possible permutation of that. “Shifting the centre of action off the player at times required a lot of careful thought too — if a cop is doing a stop-and-search on another criminal in the world, how do they behave if you commit a crime in front of them?” vice president of design Stephen Donkin explained. “Do they switch their attention to you? Do they compare the severity of the crime? If they come after you, what does the original criminal do? Does he drive off? What happens if you follow him? “Every event, encounter, interaction had to be considered with this level of depth, as there are so many possible inputs to any given situation, and every new feature or mechanic that is added becomes a new input we must collectively consider.” It’s astounding that Rockstar managed to keep this level of detail consistent over a full playthrough. Even 140 hours in, I’m still seeing new things and being blown away by the level of reactivity in every facet of the world, from Jason’s “mmm, chicken” when he kissed Lucia while she was tucking into off-brand KFC, to the police calling off a stop and search because I pulled my in-game phone out to record them. GTA 6 is a towering achievement made by a development team of perfectionists, and we likely won’t see anything quite like it until Rockstar does it again. items.title: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety
items.content_text: I'm relationship-maxxing GTA 6. Forget the money, the cars, or building a criminal empire. My main aim is to make Jason and Lucia so disgustingly loved up that NPCs violently vomit as we walk past being all cute together. I want them to be the perfect couple. I want romance. I want devotion. I want the sort of relationship that makes everyone else in Vice City feel deeply inadequate. Unfortunately, the nuanced way GTA 6 tracks even the smallest actions has turned me into a paranoid lunatic, constantly worrying that one wrong move will destroy my carefully cultivated romance. Case in point: a $6 beer that sent me into a cascade of disasters, petty crime, and emotional turmoil, eventually ending with me restarting an entire mission because I was worried I'd blown it. And honestly? I love it. Early on in the game, you're given the chance to prepare the house and complete some simple objectives ahead of picking Lucia up from prison. Naturally, I did them all. Fixed the steps, bought the necklace, got the flowers. I even made sure the car was dent-free, had a haircut and a shower, and dressed my Jason in his best jeans and shirt. My man was going to look presentable when he picked up the love of his life. I was on my best behavior. Nothing was going to stop me getting to my girl. In fact, I was so determined to be the perfect boyfriend that I even avoided committing any crimes on the way to the prison. In Grand Theft Auto. I obeyed traffic laws. I stopped at red lights. I avoided trouble wherever possible, to the point that when a random NPC tried to mug me, I just handed over my cash rather than risk getting into a fight. Remember that last part. It's important. After picking Lucia up from prison, you head straight to the Rusty Anchor for a few drinks. So far, so good. We've got the flowers, the necklace, the freshly showered boyfriend. This is going brilliantly. Then Lucia wanders off for a moment and asks Jason to get her a drink. Shit. I have no money. Suddenly, my decision to be a law-abiding citizen has come back to bite me in the arse. I gave all my money to a mugger because I was trying to be a good boyfriend, and now I can't afford to buy my girlfriend a beer. A beer that costs just $6. Surely this is a relationship test? If I follow Lucia without her drink, am I getting a little broken heart icon? Is this going into some invisible ledger of romantic failures? Have I already failed as a boyfriend, future husband, and potential co-parent because I can't produce one lousy alcoholic beverage? I start looking for solutions. I check every bottle in the bar, hoping I can just grab one and pretend I've paid for it. They're all empty. I search the entire building for something I could quickly pawn, like a trading card, or even just some random cash someone has carelessly left lying around. Nothing. The panic is setting in. I head outside and start searching the nearby streets. I don't want a wanted rating, because surely being arrested while Lucia waits patiently for a drink isn't going to do wonders for our relationship either. So I look for cars with trunks I can break into easily. I find a selection of sunglasses and hats, which is lovely, but unless Lucia has suddenly developed a taste for drinking accessories, they're not going to help me. I'm now seriously considering mugging someone. I only need $6. Six. Dollars. That's barely a crime, right? In the grand scheme of GTA, that's practically community service. I pull out my gun and start advancing on a random NPC walking down the sidewalk. I'm about to threaten an innocent stranger with a deadly weapon so I can buy my girlfriend a beer. This is what love looks like, apparently. And then it happens. The game suddenly switches to a cutscene of Lucia saying, "You forgot about me?" NO. NO! The opposite! I was thinking about you the entire time! I needed $6 for a beer, light of my life! I was prepared to commit armed robbery for you! Does that mean nothing? But the damage is done. Or at least, I think the damage is done, which is somehow worse. Has the game registered that I wandered off and abandoned Lucia? Does she think Jason is an inconsiderate arsehole? Have I just knocked several invisible points off my perfect relationship score? Is this going to come back to haunt me 30 hours from now when she remembers that time I left her alone in a bar? I can't take the risk. I restart the checkpoint. Unfortunately, this creates another problem. The checkpoint puts me right outside the prison, which means I still have no money. I've travelled back in time, but I haven't solved the fundamental issue of being a broke boyfriend. Luckily, there's a parking lot nearby. This time, I abandon my commitment to good behaviour. I go rogue, breaking open trunks left and right, ignoring alarms and grabbing whatever I can get my hands on. The same man who was carefully obeying traffic laws 20 minutes ago is now systematically robbing parked cars in broad daylight. Eventually, I walk away with $30. A fortune. Five beers' worth of romantic security. I get Lucia her drink. Crisis averted. Relationship saved. Probably. And that's the thing about GTA 6 that's completely got its hooks into me. I've become so thoroughly relationship-pilled that I'm making decisions I would never normally consider in a Grand Theft Auto game. I'm not thinking about how much money I can make, how many cars I can steal, or how much chaos I can cause. I'm thinking about whether Jason is being a good boyfriend. I'm worrying about whether Lucia feels appreciated. I'm committing crimes not for personal gain, but in the service of being a thoughtful romantic partner. It's ridiculous, but it's also fascinating. Rockstar has somehow made me care about the smallest interactions between these two characters to the point where I'm second-guessing everything I do. The possibility that an apparently insignificant action might have consequences for their relationship is enough to make even buying a beer feel like a high-stakes decision. And the uncertainty is part of what makes it work. I don't know whether failing to buy Lucia that drink would actually have mattered. Maybe she wouldn't have cared. Maybe the game wouldn't have registered it at all. But the fact that I believed it might matter was enough to completely change how I played. That's a pretty remarkable achievement for a game where I can also steal a sports car and drive it directly into the ocean. Of course, if I'm already this emotionally compromised over a $6 beer, I dread to think what will happen when Rockstar inevitably throws some huge, emotionally devastating choices at Jason and Lucia later in the narrative. Although, at this point, choosing between love and betrayal might actually be easier than figuring out how to pay for a round of drinks. Rockstar, you absolute bastards. You've made me into a person who will commit armed robbery rather than disappoint his girlfriend, and somehow you've made it feel romantic. Romance options in games are never going to feel quite the same again.
items.title_en: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety

items.title: The Official Lord of the Rings Pizza Cutter Drops to a New Low Price at Amazon
items.content_text: Amazon's Black Friday sale is a great time to find discounts on things you actually need. It's also a great time to buy expensive gifts for yourself that you absolutely don't need. Somewhere in between those two extremes is where I like to do most of my online window shopping, which is what led me to this discount on the official Lord of the Rings Pizza Wheel. Amazon is currently offering a 20% discount, which drops the price down to $159.99 for the first time ever. It's a very expensive pizza cutter for sure, but it's also one of the coolest LOTR gifts for your kitchen you'll find anywhere. As someone who makes a lot of pizzas at home, I can attest to how important it is to have a good pizza cutter at your disposal. If you don't have a sharp enough blade, toppings get crushed and pepperonis do that thing where they disappear into the cracks of every cut. You're only going to get good pizza slices if you have a knife capable of cutting good slices. Dalstrong, the brand who makes this product, uses high-quality German X50CrMoV15 steel for their knives and pizza cutters. This gives them solid toughness and corrosion resistance that will help keep the blade sharper for longer. This type of steel isn't going to hold an edge nearly as long as the high-end Japanese variety, but it's fairly easy to sharpen and hone at home if the edge does get dull. Just don't go putting it in the dishwasher! As for the LOTR stuff that actually makes this pizza cutter cool, there's a lot to love in the design. The handle is made of ebony wood and copper accents with the Leaf of Lórien carved into it. The blade itself is left bare to ensure drag-free cutting, but both sides include different designs etched into the steel. On one side you get silhouettes of the members of The Fellowship of the Ring and on the other side you get an inscription written in Elvish. I can't actually read Elvish, but I hope it just says pizza multiple times. The pizza wheel also comes with a collector's pin and a leather sheath to help protect the blade. The whole thing ships in the kind of premium gift packaging that you'd expect from a nearly $200 pizza cutter. The 4K Movie Trilogy Is Also on Sale Today Amazon also has a great deal on the 4K collection going on right now that's worth checking out. This includes both the theatrical and extended editions of the film in full 4K UHD. If you're only streaming these movies with an HBO Max subscription, you're missing out on the full visual experience.

items.excerpt: Lexie Shoaibi, the actor who plays Mandy in GTA 6, is speaking out now that the game has been officially released worldwide.
items.content_text: Lexie Shoaibi, the actor who plays Mandy in GTA 6, is speaking out now that the game has been officially released worldwide. GTA 6 is finally here, and players have wasted no time looking up the actors behind some of its colorful cast of characters. As the days go on, more and more performers are revealing that they played a part in the game — and one of these is going particularly viral due to a mystery surrounding their character. The actor who plays Mandy, a character players encounter early in the game, identified herself as Lexie Shoaibi, an American model and actress based out of New York. She posted the news on her Instagram account on November 19, where she revealed that she provided both Mandy’s voice and motion capture. “She’s a lot of fun, so if you play the game, let me know if you find me,” she said. In another post , Shoabi thanked Rockstar for casting her in the game, writing, “Y’all there aren’t words!!!! Thank you so much for the love and support. This is crazy!! Ily forever!” Warning: Spoilers for GTA 6 ahead. Turn back now if you want to remain unspoiled! Mandy is a character who’s been put under the microscope due to a few odd details that players noticed in her home. If you’ve played the first few hours of the game, you’ll know that Jason gets called over to collect rent from Mandy, who says she won’t pay up until her sink is unclogged. Jason finds the source of the clog — all while fending off aggressive romantic advances from Mandy — which appears to be a human fingerbone. Mandy snatches it from Jason’s hand and runs off with it before he can get a good look at what it really is. A quick stroll through her home and backyard show even more disturbing bits, such as a body-sized hole in the back garden and tubs of acid. The trunk of her car has also been packed with tools that could feasibly be used to kidnap or kill a victim. With all this in mind, fans are convinced that Mandy is actually a serial killer who seduces her victims. (Jason’s loyalty to Lucia really paid off!) Commenters were quick to praise Shoabi for her performance as Mandy and joke about her uncomfortable, one-sided crush on Jason, with one joking, “Why’d you do that to a committed man?” “BRO. You had me in a chokehold, but I have to stay loyal to Lucia. Sorry Mandy!!” another said. “Mandy listen… Look, I know we got off on the wrong foot, ok? Give me another chance,” another wrote. If the serial killer theory is true, it means she might not be the only murderer around; fans also spotted references to Dexter in the game, prompting even more curiosity as to Mandy’s true intentions. items.title: GTA 6 Triggers Busiest Traffic Day in Comcast History
items.excerpt: Comcast has said GTA 6's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963.
items.content_text: Comcast has said GTA 6 's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963. The latest record broken by Rockstar Games' latest actually comes from one of the biggest media and technology companies in the United States. After previously reporting that Grand Theft Auto had led to a 4x increase in traffic on Xbox consoles November 18, Comcast has now confirmed that pre-loads for the day resulted in the busiest day it has ever seen – and it wasn't close. Comcast recorded peak traffic 31% higher than the average day and 9.6% higher than the previous record holder. Moreover, GTA 6 has resulted in five out of 10 of the busiest days the network has ever seen. Even more remarkable is the news that, as reported by Comcast, 24% of all of its internet traffic during peak times was from users downloading and playing the game. If Rockstar fans weren't playing GTA 6, they were watching it. Twitch traffic increased by almost 50% on November 18 and is continuing to rise in the days following that launch. GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, but thanks to the New Zealand trick , a massive chunk of players actually took their trip to Leonida hours early. It certainly helped boost traffic across the board, and in Comcast's case, it resulted in its busiest day ever. To put some of these numbers into perspective, the company shared a very relevant measurement. November 18 traffic generated on PlayStation and Xbox alone delivered enough data for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K… for two days straight. It's shocking to see how GTA 6 affected Comcast, but then again, we've known Rockstar's new game would be a juggernaut when it eventually launched. The developer's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, reported that it had earned an unbelievable $3.79 billion in the first day after its release. That makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time, but the biggest entertainment launch across any medium . Critics everywhere helped GTA 6 earn the title of highest-rated game of all time . IGN was included in that list after delivering a 10/10 review . We said, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played." items.title: Percy Jackson Actors Reveal They Watched Attack on Titan Fan Edits to Help Themselves Cry While Filming Emotional Scenes
items.excerpt: Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
items.content_text: Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians. Attack on Titan is one of the most popular anime series in the world, in no small part due to its tragic storylines and brutal, gory battles. It’s been more than a decade since the anime first released in 2013, and fans have been making AMVs of their favorite characters ever since — but these fans probably didn’t know that their creations would help high-profile actors tap into their emotions. Speaking at 92NY on a live episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, Walker Scobell revealed his unique method for getting himself into an emotional state in preparation for sad scenes while filming Percy Jackson and the Olympians . Scobell said that he would watch fan-made edits for Eren and Mikasa, two of Attack on Titan’s main characters, set to the opening song of Season 3, Red Swan. “I was trying to get sad. I was in school, and I snuck my phone in. I was like, ‘What can I do to make myself cry?’ I searched up a bunch of — and he did the exact same thing, and we just figured this out yesterday,” Scobell said, pointing to co-star Aryan Simhadri. “We didn’t communicate this at all. We just ended up doing it,” Simhardi confirmed. “I thought of the saddest thing I could, and I searched up Eren and Mikasa edits from Attack on Titan,” Scobell continued. “I started crying at school, watching them to Red Swan. And then I got there [on set], and I couldn’t do it.” Walker & Aryan saying they watch eren & mikasa edits so they can cry on set is actually frying meee 😭😭😭 https://t.co/7JgZFv91Dr — ELON SMD (@pearlinasbeau) November 20, 2026 Fans in the crowd had excited reactions to this revelation, as did fans online when clips from the episode made their way on social media shortly thereafter. “Their tragedy is so profounddd everyone can feel it… oh they really are modern day Romeo and Juliet,” one fan wrote on X/Twitter. “Red Swan is a Top 3 OP, I don’t blame him,” another said. “The way they're emotionally regulating through anime edits on a professional set is the most Gen Z actor thing I've ever heard,” another remarked. It’s no wonder that actors take notes from Attack on Titan for their own projects; in fact, Eren’s English voice actor, Bryce Papenbrook, revealed that he literally unhinged his jaw while screaming in one of the anime’s most iconic scenes in an effort to really sell the character’s pain and confusion. Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3, The Titan’s Curse , is streaming on Disney+ and Hulu right now with new episodes dropping every Friday through December 11, 2026.
